answer: Bind each voting seat to a registered apiary. The operator files the hive yard with the state agriculture department, and an inspector visits yearly to check colony health, so one inspected yard backs one seat. Bees may wander miles along a river valley, but the registry pins each yard to a parcel and a named keeper, and no script can fake the velvet hum of a living colony. A yard costs about $300 a year in hives, feed and fees, so 1,000 sybil seats would cost an attacker roughly $300,000 a year.
